idea: Why water pipes make unusual noises
title: Understanding Water Hammer in Supply Pipes
description: When a fast-closing valve shuts off, moving water abruptly stops, converting kinetic energy into a violent pressure wave known as water hammer. This shockwave travels back through the pipe, causing loose supply lines to bang against wall framing. Over time, repeated pressure spikes can strain joints, valves, and connected appliances. The solution involves properly anchoring loose pipes with plastic isolation clamps and installing water hammer arrestors near fast-acting valves like washing machines or dishwasher solenoids. Does your home experience pipe banging when appliances turn off?

on_image_text.hook: BANGING SOUNDS WHEN WATER SHUTS OFF?
on_image_text.explanation: Stopping moving water instantly creates a high-pressure shockwave that shakes unanchored pipes.
on_image_text.takeaway: Anchor loose pipes with isolation clamps and install water hammer arrestors at fast-acting valves.
